thread:
incident-bot: PAGER: GPU node instability detected on `gpu-nv14-07` — multiple Xid 13/31 resets and container restarts. Severity: P1. Affected service: inference-runtime-prod. Paging oncall: @matt-oncall. Please ACK and triage. :rotating_light:

matt-oncall: ACK. jumping on it. any customer visible errors yet?

adria-eng: seeing increased 5xxs from the runtime, some requests hang then fail. metric spike in driver-reset count -> 27 in last 5m. pushing logs now.

kate-infra: I can see node `gpu-nv14-07` reporting ECC corrected error counters incrementing and NVML driver reset events in syslog. prepping cordon.

matt-oncall: cordon+drain plan: cordon node, move low-priority pods, restart inference containers on other nodes. will keep one replica to debug. executing: `kubectl cordon gpu-nv14-07 && kubectl drain gpu-nv14-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline paused due to node cordon. Notifying subsystems.

adria-eng: logs from failing container attached: ```
[2026-03-15T18:02:10Z] runtime: kernel reported Xid 31 NVGPU_RESET
[2026-03-15T18:02:10Z] container: oom_kill? no, container restarted by kubelet
[2026-03-15T18:02:11Z] inference: tokenizer still running but response stream cut
```

tilly-sre: running quick health checks: `nvidia-smi -q -a` shows ECC errors (Volatile) rising, GPU temperature within normal, driver 525.85.12, kernel 6.1. Command and partial output: ```
# nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,ecc.errors.volatile.uncorrected --format=csv
0, NVIDIA A40, 0
1, NVIDIA A40, 0
2, NVIDIA A40, 12
3, NVIDIA A40, 0
```

kate-infra: posting dmesg tail: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (31) 00000000
[ 12345.679002] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:86:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679110] nvidia 0000:86:00.0: GPU reset failed
```

matt-oncall: initial mitigation done: node cordoned, most pods drained. One inference pod left for live debugging. Routing policy: failover to dedicated pool for new requests. Customer-facing impact: intermittent 5-10% error rate for real-time inference for ~10m. Jess, can you flag any high-revenue customers?

jess-cs: flagged two customers on trial and one enterprise account with live traffic. Notifying them: "We’re investigating transient GPU node instability causing intermittent inference errors. No data loss. Engineers are performing live mitigation."

adria-eng: attaching kernel oops excerpt and core logs; looks like a driver reset loop on GPU slot 2. Suggest rebooting node after collecting full logs.

tilly-sre: running `sudo cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params` and capturing `syslog` and `kdump` in case of full OOPS. Also increasing driver log level.

kate-infra: recommendation: reimage node with driver rollback to 520.x to test; 525 has a known instability on this microcode revision. I'll prep a replacement node and schedule controlled reboot.

matt-oncall: agree. plan: keep node offline for now, reprovision replacement from pool, cordon remains. If replacement stable, we'll rotate others. ETA for reprovision ~20 minutes.

incident-bot: Status update posted to incident channel and paging logs. Incident timer: 00:22 elapsed.

adria-eng: quick check: can we collect NVML stacks from the hung process? attaching steps: `gdb -p $(pidof inference-runtime)` then `thread apply all bt` — might need to keep prod pod alive for 10-15s.

matt-oncall: did that, got stack showing NVML call in loop, capturing upload to internal S3: `s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1950012345/` .

kate-infra: replacement node `gpu-nv14-17` up with driver 520.56.09 and joined cluster. Running smoke: small throughput tests OK, no driver resets in 5m.

adria-eng: routing traffic back to pool with gradual ramp. Monitoring for Xid spikes.

matt-oncall: ramp to 30% traffic -> 5xxs drop, driver reset count holding steady. Marking `gpu-nv14-07` for forensic reimage and kernel dump analysis.

jess-cs: Sent update to affected customers with ETA for full postmortem. No customer reported data loss.

tilly-sre: notes for handoff: collected `dmesg`, `syslog`, `nvidia-smi -q`, core dump, kdump, and uploaded to S3. Suspected cause: driver+firmware mismatch causing Xid loop under specific memory access pattern -> further analysis required.

matt-oncall: handing off to @tilly-sre for overnight monitoring and follow-up. Next oncall @kate-infra will be informed if node reimage starts. Handoff notes: actions taken, logs path, customer list, replacement node id. Handoff time: 00:40 from start.

tilly-sre: ACKed. I'll keep a watch window 0-6h, update if any regression. If Xid resets reappear, escalate to driver vendor and initiate coordinated upgrade plan.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigating -> partial recovery. Severity downgraded to P2. Postmortem requested. :white_check_mark:
